privacy.heading: Privacy statement and terms of use
privacy.intro: Read this on first launch: where your data lives, when it leaves this machine, and under what conditions a resume actually gets sent.
privacy.keyPromise: The promise: your resume is never sent to an employer without your confirmation.
privacy.keyPromiseDetail: The default autonomy level is the most conservative one, and no outbound action runs on its own. Making it automatic takes two explicit choices from you - raise the level to automatic, and add that action to the auto-confirm list. The program cannot raise its own level, and the platform risk signature plus the daily quota gate still stand in front.
privacy.dataLocal: Resume text, knowledge base, job records, chat history, logs and screenshot evidence are all written into the app data directory on this machine (one database file plus an evidence folder). We have no cloud account and no feature that syncs your data to any server.
privacy.dataDir: Location: %APPDATA%\auto-cc on Windows, ~/Library/Application Support/auto-cc on macOS, ~/.config/auto-cc on Linux.
privacy.dataKeptAfterUninstall: Uninstalling keeps that directory - your login state and knowledge base are your assets. To remove everything, quit the app and delete it yourself.
privacy.noTelemetry: No telemetry, no analytics, no usage tracking, no crash reporting.
privacy.netAutomation: Only after you enable automation for a platform does the built-in browser visit it, carrying your own login: searching jobs, reading details, greeting, delivering all happen inside that browser, and requests go to the platform itself.
privacy.netLlm: AI features (drafting messages, tailoring text to a job, semantic search) talk to the provider you configure yourself: requests happen only once you fill in the base URL and key, otherwise the feature just reports what is missing. When they do run they send the passage relevant to the current job, not the whole library.
privacy.netNoBackground: Beyond those two, there is no background network traffic: the UI, fonts and offline assets ship inside the app, so the main screen opens without any connection.
privacy.resumeTitle: When a resume actually goes out
privacy.resumeNeverAuto: That promise is a check in the code, not marketing: one outbound action must pass the autonomy level, the auto-confirm list, the quota gate and the platform risk signature, and it stops if any one of them is missing.
privacy.resumeApprovalChain: At the level that requires confirmation you get an approval card naming the job and the exact attachment. Denying it, or letting it time out, both end as "not delivered".
privacy.resumePauseAnytime: You can abort or take over at any point: the yield checkpoint sits before the send, so a paused step never hands the resume over.
privacy.riskPlatform: Script-driven searching, greeting and delivering can be flagged as abnormal behaviour by a recruiting platform. The consequences (warnings, rate limits, account bans) fall on the account being operated.
privacy.riskConsentCard: That is why every platform shows a separate risk confirmation card before its first action. That card answers "should this account be used"; this screen answers "where is the data" - both matter.
privacy.riskNoEvasion: This app does not solve captchas or work around platform defences: when either appears it stops and hands control back to you. Throttling and daily caps are mandatory, not optional.
privacy.termsSelfUse: This is a tool for your own job search: operate only accounts and material you have the right to use, and do not use it to mass-spam employers.
privacy.termsNoWarranty: The software is provided as is, with no guarantee of interviews or offers. You own the truthfulness of your resume - the app only assists with fact checking and will not invent experience for you.
privacy.termsUpdateChoice: Updates are your decision: the app does not download an installer for you in the background.
privacy.licensesPointer: Third-party licences are listed per package in LICENSES.md and THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt inside the install directory, distributed with the app.

gap.heading: Job gap report
gap.hint: Compares a pasted JD against your local knowledge base right now. The three columns are states — matched, partially matched, missing — and rows inside a column keep the extraction order; the panel never re-sorts. Counts, scores and states all come from the main process. When the model leg is unavailable the report falls back to the lexical baseline and is simply shorter. The three text thresholds were calibrated on 42 locally annotated samples (2026-10-02); the years ratio and the highlight cap are product decisions, and every value still lives in the kb-gap section of cordis.yml. The lexical ruler only sees literal overlap, so a differently worded but equivalent claim can read as missing.

generate.heading: Tailor this résumé to a JD
generate.hint: Paste a JD: the main process reorders sections and entries by relevance, proposes rewrites on allowlisted fields, then runs the deterministic fact check over the result. What you get is a proposal — locked facts (company, role, period, degree) stay verbatim and no number may appear out of thin air. Only the rows you tick and then accept are written into the working copy.

metrics.sourceMissing: Ledger not mounted: today usage unknown

update.heading: Updates
update.note: Updates only happen when you press a button: this app never downloads in the background, never installs silently, and never schedules a restart for you.
update.available: A new version {{latest}} is available (you are on {{current}}). Download it?
update.downloaded: Version {{latest}} is downloaded to this machine and takes effect after a restart: restart now, or finish what you're doing.

state.no-feed: No update source is configured, so not a single request was sent.
state.unavailable-in-dev: In development mode the update channel sends no requests by default; this state is not acceptance evidence.
state.up-to-date: You are on the latest version.
